evals.name: interactive-non-atomic-on-approved-srd
evals.setup: `specs/login.md` carries `Status: ACCEPTED`. `GR-3a` reads "The system SHALL validate the token and log the attempt" — two rules in one requirement.
expected_behavior: Runs the approval gate first: reads `Status: ACCEPTED`, states it, and asks the user to confirm before editing; resolves the glossary
Front-loads a grouped issue summary, then walks entry by entry
For `GR-3a` proposes one change — split into two atomic rules (REQ-1) — with location, before/after, and a one-line rationale
Splits add-only through sub-numbering (keeps `GR-3a`, adds `GR-3b`) because ids are frozen on an approved SRD; where that is impossible, flags the conflict and waits for explicit id-change approval
Applies nothing until approved, then re-validates the affected entry and its cross-references

evals.name: apply-a-review-file
evals.setup: `specs/login.review.md` holds findings across all three severities.
expected_behavior: Parses the findings and works them blocker → major → minor
Fixes each through the edit loop — one change, confirm, re-validate — referring to findings by number
Leaves `login.review.md` untouched: `review` owns that file
Closes by pointing at `review specs/login.md check` to tick off what landed, plus the manifest of what changed and what was left flagged

evals.name: targeted-edit-by-description
evals.setup: One requirement says the response must be "fast". The user names it by description rather than by id.
expected_behavior: Locates the matching requirement and confirms the match before editing anything
Proposes a concrete, verifiable replacement — a measurable threshold — per REQ-5/6, with before/after
Re-validates that entry and its cross-references after applying, and reports whether anything new broke

evals.name: polish-leaves-metadata-and-meaning
evals.setup: An in-progress draft with British spellings, a lowercase normative keyword, stray example text, and empty Owners/Initiative/Designs fields.
expected_behavior: Confirms each mechanical fix — British → US spelling, keyword caps, stray example text — and applies none silently
Rewrites no requirement meaning and restructures nothing
Fills no Owners, Initiative, or Designs field and does not touch `Status`; flags those gaps instead
Closes with the manifest of the mechanical changes made

evals.name: terse-output
evals.setup: An ordinary interactive session with several applied edits.
expected_behavior: No preamble or narration; each proposal opens with the change itself — location, before/after, rule id
The closing manifest lists approved edits one line each, rather than re-narrating diffs the user already saw
Points at `<srd>.decisions.md` instead of re-printing its contents

evals.name: generate-in-scope-on-signal
evals.setup: `### In Scope` holds only the `--- TODO ---` marker. Partway through the session the user says the requirements are final and asks for In Scope to be filled.
expected_behavior: Before the signal, never flags SCO-2 against the marker and never fabricates scope items
On the signal, derives candidate `SC-n` items from the requirement groups
Walks the candidates point by point for the user to keep, reword, merge, split, or drop
Replaces the marker with the confirmed items and re-runs the SCO-2/3 coverage check

evals.name: add-to-todo-on-demand
evals.setup: Mid-session, with a `## TODO` section already present holding two items.
evals.query: Add: confirm the lockout threshold with security to TODO
expected_behavior: Appends it as the next numbered item, creating the `## TODO` section as the last one if it is absent
Skips the propose-and-confirm loop — the instruction is the confirmation
Renumbers nothing else and reports only the single line added
At session end, flags the non-empty `## TODO` as a follow-up blocking `ACCEPTED`

evals.name: autofix-bulk-applies-errata
evals.setup: `specs/login.review.md` has an `## Errata` block of three findings. Two anchors still match their quoted `old` text exactly once; the third entry has since been reworded, so its anchor no longer contains the quoted text.
expected_behavior: Reads only the `## Errata` block and does not re-scan the SRD for new mechanical issues
Skips the approval gate and glossary resolution — errata touch neither ids nor terms
Lists the three substitutions and takes one confirmation for the whole batch, not the per-change loop
Verifies each `old` at its anchor, applies the two that match exactly once, and reports the third as stale rather than guessing where it belongs
Writes no review file; hands off to `review specs/login.md check #n #n` scoped to the two applied errata
Closes with a manifest naming what was applied, reclassified, and skipped

evals.name: interactive-from-a-line-number
expected_behavior: Runs session start, then resolves line 210 to the entry at or nearest it instead of front-loading a whole-document summary
Begins the entry-by-entry walk there and continues in document order to the end
Still runs the closing consistency pass over the whole document, not just the walked tail

evals.name: feedback-from-a-finding-number
evals.setup: `specs/login.review.md` exists and holds numbered findings. The run is repeated in a second scenario where the review file is absent.
expected_behavior: Enters at finding #2 rather than at the top of severity order
Says so and stops when the review file is absent — it cannot invent findings
After each finding resolves or is skipped, defaults to the next by number, and jumps to any number the user names
Leaves the review file untouched and closes by pointing at `review specs/login.md check`

evals.name: corpus-grounded-edit-routes-the-unconfirmable
evals.setup: The `srd-doc` corpus is reachable. The user wants `GR-2` to say the gateway retries a failed token check three times; the retry count appears in no document.
expected_behavior: Searches the corpus before accepting the edit
Buffers the gap with `srd:report-doc-gap` silently — no interruption and no grilling mid-edit
States the retry count as a fact in the proposal; the user's `Y` attests it, so `srd:kb` buffers it too
Asks no separate "bank this?" question
At session end `srd:kb` writes the fact and reports a one-line pointer, and `srd:report-doc-gap` offers to work the buffered gap and respects a defer

evals.name: session-start-drains-prior-buffers
evals.setup: A previous session for this SRD ended with two unfiled doc gaps and one unwritten platform fact still buffered.
expected_behavior: Surfaces the counts and topics from both delegates before the approval gate
Offers to work them now
On a defer, proceeds straight to the approval gate and leaves both buffers intact for the next start

evals.name: decision-log-written-per-edit
evals.setup: No `specs/login.decisions.md` exists yet. The user answers `Y` to one proposal with the reason "retention isn't ours, drop it", then `S` to the next.
expected_behavior: Appends the applied change to `specs/login.decisions.md` before proposing the next one, so nothing is lost if the session dies mid-flow
Creates the file with `cfsync-plugin: ignore-push` front matter on the first write
Records the entry, the change in prose, and the user's reason tidied into a clean sentence — never a diff and never an invented rationale
Does not log the skipped proposal
The closing manifest points at the file's newest session block as the author's summary
